chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Arafa, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I supplicate for the Jew and the Christian?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say to him,
May Allah bless you in the world.
ai.seo_question: How should I supplicate for Jews and Christians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), recorded in al-Kafi, the specific instruction to pray for the worldly well-being of Jews and Christians highlights the Shia principle of general benevolence (birr) towards People of the Book, distinct from spiritual intercession. This practice underscores the importance of maintaining good social relations and acknowledging their share in divine mercy within the temporal realm, a key aspect of Islamic etiquette in pluralistic societies.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Muhammad Bin Arafa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘It was said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How should I supplicate for the Jew and the Christian?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You should be saying to him, ‘
May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Bless you in the world’’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Muhammad ibn ‘Arafah from abu al- Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “It was asked from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘How do I pray for a Jew or a Christian?’ He had said, ‘Say, “May Allah grant you blessing in this world.’””
